blocks.text: Lesson 8 — Secure web applications and OWASP risks

LEARNING OUTCOME
Protect web requests, authorization, sessions, data queries, output and dependencies.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

A web app receives input, authenticates the caller, authorizes the action, applies business rules, accesses data and returns a response. Security belongs at every stage. Client-side checks improve experience but can be bypassed, so validate on the server with expected formats and limits.

blocks.text: Check permissions on every sensitive request and scope each data query to the signed-in identity or approved role. Use secure session settings, rotate session IDs after sign-in, set appropriate Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite cookie attributes, and avoid exposing tokens in URLs.

blocks.caption: Visual 3/6 — Authorize action. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 4/6 — Secure session. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Encode untrusted output for its context, use parameterized database queries, apply CSRF protection where relevant, keep dependencies updated and avoid verbose production errors. Use code review, threat modeling and testing before launch; use monitoring after deployment.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.output: Toy validation only; never use a client-side check as the only authorization.

blocks.question: Why is client-side validation not enough?
options: A client can be changed or bypassed, so the server must validate too
blocks.explanation: The server is the trusted enforcement point for input and permissions.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What prevents a user from accessing another user’s record?
options: Server-side authorization on each protected request
blocks.explanation: Permissions must be enforced on the server for each sensitive action.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: Which approach better protects private information?
options: Copy all customer records for convenience
Use synthetic data and collect only necessary, authorized evidence
blocks.explanation: Data minimization and redaction reduce privacy and exposure risks.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What is a sound step after applying a fix?
options: Retest the same authorized condition and document the result
blocks.explanation: Retesting verifies the correction and preserves a useful record.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What should happen when a target is outside scope?
options: Stop and ask the owner to clarify permission
blocks.explanation: Scope is a boundary; do not proceed without permission.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.
